subject: MAP & Eval: Commit milestones, pricing bands, and cross-region failover
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@blueharborhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + eval plan — commit bands, residency premium, cross-region failover

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an evaluation cadence that maps to commercial milestones. High level:

- 30-day technical evaluation (pilot) to validate latency + throughput in your primary region (us-west-2).
- Ramp phase (months 2–4) where we recommend a measured commit to Dedicated capacity as you move to sustained load.
- Commercial milestones tied to commit bands that unlock discounts and lower region/residency premiums.

Key commercial points in this draft:
- Pricing bands: 0–50k tokens/day (no commit) | 50k–500k tokens/day (mid commit) | 500k+ tokens/day (enterprise commit). Discounts increase with higher committed s-usage.
- Data residency premium: baseline +12% for multi-region data residency enforcement (additional regions that guarantee data staying in-region). This premium covers: separate region capacity, KMS per-region, and additional audit attestations.
- Cross-region failover: standard for Hosted customers is best-effort; for Dedicated we offer an optional cross-region failover add-on (standby capacity) at +7% of committed spend. If a customer purchases a 12-month commit with Dedicated, we can discuss reducing that to +4% depending on standby capacity guarantees.

Action items proposed in MAP (attached):
1) Sign evaluation SOW (30d) by May 26 to start pilot week of June 2.
2) Technical kickoff + access to test model in us-west-2.
3) By pilot completion, provide telemetry/acceptance criteria to apply commit band pricing.

Questions for you before I send this to procurement/your legal:
- Is a 12% residency premium in the ballpark of expectations for Blue Harbor, or should we model a tiered residency premium based on number of additional regions?
- Do you expect cross-region failover to be soft (best-effort) for Hosted, or must it be contractual with an SLA (we can do this via Dedicated/standby pools)?

Attached: BlueHarbor_MAP_v3.pdf (draft MAP + timelines)

If the high-level looks good I’ll loop in Legal + Finance for a redline on the commercial terms.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the clear plan and the MAP. A few things we need clarified before I push to procurement and legal:

- Residency premium: can you provide the breakdown of what the +12% covers (ops, KMS, audit tooling)? Would Blue Harbor be able to reduce that if we limit to one additional DR region vs. multi-region?
- Cross-region failover: important for our DR posture. Is that +7% charged on committed spend or on standby capacity (e.g., reserved instances)? Are there options to cap that charge if we only need a single failover region?
- Commit ramp discounts: can you show an example TCO if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated contract at the mid vs. enterprise band?

Procurement also asked for: sample redline of the commercial clause (pricing table + residency language) and a stub SOW showing acceptance criteria for the pilot.

Appreciate it — Danielle

Subject: RE: MAP draft + eval plan — internal pricing/terms suggestion

Team — internal notes for the proposed commercial responses to Blue Harbor:

Summary of negotiation levers (we should align Sales + Legal + Finance):
- Residency premium: make this tiered by "extra DR regions": +6% for one additional region (full residency guarantees), +10% for two, +12% for three or more. This gives the customer a path to lower premium as they constrain DR scope.
- Cross-region failover: two commercial options:
  * Option A (Dedicated standby): Standby capacity included as a % of committed spend (default +7%). Can cap to single failover region at +4% for enterprise commits >$X/month.
  * Option B (On-demand failover): No standby charge but a per-hour consumption uplift when failover is executed; lower baseline but weaker SLA.
- Ramp discounts: structured so that once telemetry shows 60% of target usage during month 3, customer automatically moves to next discount tier. We need to include a clear acceptance/telemetry clause in the SOW so there's no ambiguity.

Attachments: commercial_terms_redline.docx (redline with suggested residency and failover language). Please review and I'll pull Finance numbers (Marcus) for the exact thresholds and breakpoints.

Aditya

Subject: Final MAP offer + commercial terms for pilot and Dedicated ramp

Hi Danielle —

Thanks for the questions — we discussed internally and attached a final commercial proposal that maps directly to the MAP milestones. Highlights below so procurement/legal can review quickly:

1) Pilot (30 days) — no residency premium; standard Hosted pricing during pilot. Acceptance criteria captured in the attached SOW (telemetry thresholds for latency/99p tail/throughput). Pilot must be signed by May 26 to start the week of June 2.

2) Ramp / Commit bands — once pilot acceptance is met, Blue Harbor may elect one of the commit bands. Example 12-month TCO (illustrative):
   - Mid commit (50k–500k tokens/day): base price $0.0018/token → effective after 10% discount with a $X/mo commit.
   - Enterprise commit (500k+ tokens/day): base price $0.0013/token → effective after 22% discount with a $Y/mo commit.

3) Residency premiums — revised, tiered structure as discussed: +6% (one DR region), +10% (two regions), +12% (three+). If Blue Harbor signs a 12-month Dedicated commit at the enterprise band, we will cap residency premium at +4% for the first DR region as a credit.

4) Cross-region failover — two options:
   - Dedicated standby (recommended for contractual SLA): +4% (single failover region) on enterprise 12-month commits; +7% otherwise. This covers reserved standby capacity and per-region KMS configuration.
   - On-demand failover (no standby charge): triggered uplift on consumption while failover is active; lower baseline but no contractual uptime guarantee.

Next steps:
- I'll attach the redlined commercial terms and the SOW (pilot acceptance criteria). If procurement is comfortable with the tiered residency approach and the Dedicated standby option at +4% for enterprise commits, we can aim to have the SOW + MAP fully executed by June 6 to keep ramp timelines.
